_about: The narration the voice reads, Scenario 1, v3 (S294, 2026-09-26). SPOKEN FORM: acronyms are written unspaced (CPL, EDD, FTES) so each reads as one quick word, the stress on its last letter; FTES also needs the phoneme fix below, because unspaced it reads as the word 'eftess'. MAP is written 'map' so it is said as the word. Years are said the way people say them aloud (twenty twenty-six through twenty-eight; the twenty-six, twenty-seven year, whose comma keeps the two years apart) with a lighter stress on the twenties, and the Minimum conditions scene reads 'by November first', as its headline does, leaving the year to the screen (November 1, 2026). Voice: Kokoro-82M af_heart, speed 1.0, one pass per scene. Sam chose the voice (Heart); v2 read stilted on the spaced letters and the years; v3 awaits his OK. narrate.py reads this file. Each scene's `cues` name its reveals (Sam, 2026-09-27: cue each reveal to the word that names it): `at` is the reveal's film time in its scene (where it begins, or where a count lands), `word` the phrase in the text that names it, once; cues.py pins each to the moment the voice says it. A cue with `skip` stays off the clock for the reason it gives.

layout._why: The narrated cut paces each scene as its lead-in (the seam, its barrier and the first reveal), its clip, and its air; Sam, 2026-09-26: "slow down and lengthen the timing a bit to accommodate readability and narration."

scenes.text: Let's walk through how CPL Initiative funding works for twenty twenty-six through twenty-eight, and what it means for your college.

scenes.text: The state set aside thirty-five million dollars in one-time funding for the twenty-six, twenty-seven year. Just over twenty-five million of it goes straight to a hundred and eighteen institutions. The rest funds statewide CPL projects and technology, plus two Chancellor's Office positions that support colleges.

scenes.text: Every institution has a maximum allocation for the two years. It's based on the institution's share of instruction, credit and noncredit together, and it falls between a hundred and fifty thousand dollars and four hundred thousand. Sample College's maximum, for example, is about three hundred forty-five thousand.

scenes.text: That maximum splits into a credit share and a noncredit share, following each institution's own mix of instruction. And only noncredit outcomes count toward the noncredit share.

scenes.text: Three priorities carry the funding. Access counts applied CPL units from students who start at the CPL Portal, at your college's landing page, or through a batch upload. Completion counts transcribed CPL units, with the map counselor step checked. And career attainment counts CPL units for students who go on to a career outcome, which the Chancellor's Office measures through EDD wage records.

scenes.text: Each priority has a target, measured in FTES. Thirty semester units of CPL make one FTES, or forty-five if you're on the quarter system. Here's the part to remember: reach half of a target, and your college qualifies for half that share. Go past the target, and the share stays where it is. It's the ceiling.

scenes.text: Before any funding is released, your college meets three minimum conditions by November first. Name a CPL coordinator, then list that person in map and on your college's CPL landing page. Put your local confirmation of participation on file. And make sure at least seventy-five percent of your enrolled veterans have their Joint Services Transcripts uploaded in map. Until all three are met, the funding your college demonstrates is held in reserve for it.
